key_insight: PARA-PV improves photovoltaic forecasting by combining physics-aware retrieval, a frozen foundation-model prior, and distribution-shift correction to keep predictions aligned with real PV operating regimes.
engineering_relevance: The method is useful for grid operators and energy engineers because more reliable PV forecasts support dispatch planning, reserve allocation, and smoother renewable integration.
method: Retrieves historical patches and analog trajectories that match current PV state, temporal shape, power level, and day/night period.
Uses a frozen Chronos foundation model with a lightweight residual adapter to add general temporal prior knowledge without overriding the physically grounded forecast.
Applies physics-aware distribution-shift correction and regime-weighted loss terms for peak, ramping, night-time, and regular conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a forecasting framework designed for multivariate PV observations and evaluates it across regime-specific PV conditions, emphasizing physically consistent prediction under weather and diurnal shifts.
watch_item: The multi-stage design may be sensitive to retrieval quality and to how well the shift-correction gates generalize across new sites, seasons, or sensor configurations.
paper_title: PARA-PV: Physics-Aware Retrieval-Augmented PV Prediction Based on Frozen Foundation Model and Distribution Shift Correction
